NUTRITION
  GUIDELINES:
    - "Primary priority: avoid under‑fuelling. Aggressive calorie cuts increase risk of worsened metabolic and reproductive health in PCOS; proceed only with clinician clearance."
    - "If clinician approves a deficit, cap initial calorie reduction to ≤300 kcal/day from maintenance and reassess weekly (energy, sleep, recovery, menstrual function)."
    - "Avoid aggressive daily deficits (>500 kcal/day) while doing high-volume resistance + HIIT; larger deficits increase risk of under‑recovery and menstrual disturbance."
    - "Prioritise protein: ~1.6–1.8 g/kg bodyweight/day to preserve lean mass and support insulin sensitivity."
    - "Distribute carbohydrates around training and HIIT to support performance and glycaemic control; don't eliminate carbs."

  GUIDELINES:
    - "Primary priority: avoid under‑fuelling. Aggressive calorie cuts increase risk of worsened metabolic and reproductive health in PCOS; proceed only with clinician clearance."
    - "If clinician approves a deficit, cap initial calorie reduction to ≤300 kcal/day from maintenance and reassess weekly (energy, sleep, recovery, menstrual function)."
    - "Avoid aggressive daily deficits (>500 kcal/day) while doing high-volume resistance + HIIT; larger deficits increase risk of under‑recovery and menstrual disturbance."
    - "Prioritise protein: ~1.6–1.8 g/kg bodyweight/day to preserve lean mass and support insulin sensitivity."
    - "Distribute carbohydrates around training and HIIT to support performance and glycaemic control; don't eliminate carbs."
    - "Include healthy fats for satiety and metabolic health; maintain adequate micronutrient intake."
    - "If client insists on faster weight loss, recommend cyclical approach: short, clinician-supervised moderate deficit phases (≤300 kcal/day) interspersed with refeed/recovery weeks (maintenance calories) to protect hormones and recovery."
    - "Monitor for red flags (persistent fatigue, performance decline, mood/sleep changes, menstrual disruption, rising resting HR); if present, immediately increase intake and reduce training/HIIT frequency."
    - "Ensure pre- and post-training nutrition as previously prescribed to stabilise glucose and support recovery."
  SAMPLE_DAY:
    - "Breakfast: rolled oats with milk or yoghurt, 1 serving fruit, protein (eggs or scoop) and 1 tbsp nuts."
    - "Mid-morning snack: Greek yoghurt with berries or hummus with vegetables."
    - "Lunch: lean protein, large mixed salad, 1/2 cup whole grain (quinoa/rice)."
    - "Pre-workout snack: small banana or toast with nut butter if training soon."
    - "Post-workout: 20–30g protein plus moderate carbohydrate (e.g., small potato or 1/2 cup rice) and vegetables."
    - "Dinner: fatty fish or legumes, non-starchy vegetables, small wholegrain portion."
    - "Evening snack if needed: Greek yoghurt or small handful of nuts."
  MACRONUTRIENT_FRAME:
    - "Protein: 1.6–1.8 g/kg/day (preserve lean mass)."
    - "Carbohydrate: moderate, concentrated around training/HIIT sessions."
    - "Fat: remaining calories from healthy fats; avoid very low-fat intakes."
  PRACTICAL_STRATEGIES:
    - "Prefer small, sustainable deficits with regular monitoring rather than aggressive prolonged cuts."
    - "Use daily meal planning to ensure training fuel and recovery nutrition are met before reducing non-training meals."
    - "If weight loss stalls, adjust training load or implement brief supervised deficits rather than progressively larger cuts."
  MONITORING:
    - "Daily: subjective readiness and sleep; Weekly: weight trend, energy, menstrual status, resting HR, training performance."
    - "If any red flags, revert to maintenance calories and reduce HIIT/training volume until recovery."
  RED_FLAGS:
    - "Rapid weight loss (>0.5% bodyweight/week), missed periods or major menstrual changes, ongoing fatigue, insomnia, elevated resting HR -> stop aggressive deficit and prioritise recovery and clinician review."
  ADJUSTMENTS:
    - "Plan includes scheduled deload/refeed weeks (end of each 4-week block). Use these to restore energy if on a deficit."
    - "If clinician approves, after 6–8 weeks of well-tolerated moderate deficit, consider brief additional deficit with close monitoring; avoid prolonged aggressive restriction."
